Below is an essential bibliography of works focusing on the history, geography and culture of the areas touched by the Via del Cifalco and, more broadly, of the territory lying between the Taro and the Scrivia. Within it, some works deserve a special mention.

Those containing by far the most in-depth information on the Via del Cifalco are the works of Guido Ferretti (2012) and Carmen Artocchini (1973): two very important figures for local historiography, who have so much to teach with their massive scholarly output.

The photographic books by Fabrizio Capecchi are a great classic for lovers of the Apennines and have enjoyed great success over the years, helping to attract the attention of a wide public, not limited to people who already frequent these places.

The photographic books by Fabrizio Bottari, a pupil – like the present writer – of Fabrizio Capecchi, have also greatly enriched the cultural heritage of the territory. Fabrizio Bottari has carried forward the reflection of photographic books on the Levante Ligure and on the decline of rural civilisation, capturing deep nuances of the history and geography of the territories and relating them to the most contemporary issues.

In the wake of “critical” literature, the works of Alfredo Morosetti are decisive. He devoted his life to monographic studies on specific aspects of Italian rural civilisation, and of the Apennines in particular, placing the emphasis on the heritage of memory that is disappearing.

Also crucial are the works of Sandro Sbarbaro (in particular the one from 2004). The author gives us a goldmine of knowledge on the local history of Val d’Aveto and its surroundings, combining a popularising approach with methodological and scholarly authority.
